findings.title: `rules_open` identifies rules `by DECISION ID`, and the explore format defines no decision IDs
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: READ] The rung mandates rules identified by DECISION ID and the field is typed as an array of them. The format it reads from — orbit-explore-modifications:119-124 and the scaffold at explore.ts:398-416 — defines Decisions as `<dated entries; each captures what was decided and a brief rationale>`: no identifier, no slot for one. `D-rc13-16` style IDs are a convention of THIS exploration's hand-written file, not of the shipped surface, and no task introduces one. As written the rung cannot name anything for an exploration authored under the convention this change ships. Add the decision-ID slot to the format and the scaffold, or change the rung to a reference it can compute.

findings.title: No parseable grammar is specified for a Mechanism entry, so `rules_open`/`rules_total` are not computable as specified
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: EXECUTE] `derived by the emit surface from the Mechanism section's declared closure forms` names an owner but no format. explore-counter.ts:36-99 keys on TOP-LEVEL list items under `## Decisions` / `## Open questions`, fence-aware, and knows nothing else. To produce rules_open a parser must locate (a) a per-rule entry boundary, (b) its decision reference, (c) a declared closure-form token, (d) the SUPERSEDED / handed-away annotation. None has a stated shape in any requirement or task — task 2.4's exemplar is body prose, not a grammar. The prior pass's CRITICAL #4 was closed by naming the field's type and owner; the INPUT FORMAT it asked for is still absent.

findings.title: ENGINE-COMPUTED does not remove self-classification — it relocates it from the payload to the file, and an omitted rule is invisible
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: FALSIFY] The requirement argues the field must not be caller-supplied because that would be self-classification. But the engine's only input is the Mechanism section, whose contents are the author's own judgment about which Decisions are rules — and D4 makes that judgment deliberately GRAMMAR-INDEPENDENT, i.e. undetectable from the Decisions text. So rules_total counts the rules the author chose to write down; a rule never entered yields `rules_open: []` and Mature asserts readiness — the exact failure this stage exists to prevent, reachable by OMISSION rather than false declaration. Not a reason to drop the requirement (Case 8 concedes no readout would have caught this exploration's own gap), but the delta claims the loophole is closed. State the residual: the engine sees declared rules only, omission is invisible, and the cross-check is audit-drift or a later reader.

findings.title: The ADDED requirement is titled `Six moves applied per rule` and its scenario `records all six moves` while the requirement mandates EIGHT
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: COHERE] Line 3 and the scenario title at line 24 are unedited survivors of the pre-walk shape; the body says EIGHT MOVES and tables eight. findings.title: A NINTH class the eight moves lack, from this change's own record: the mechanism is correct and never runs
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: NONE] A finding about the SET, which the residual says is the right way to report it. Case 8's own finding is the evidence: `a rule that is not mechanically enforced does not get applied to the artifact that invented it` — D-rc13-7 was correct, complete and never invoked until scheduled; D-rc13-15 records the same shape. Classified against the eight: READ fine, ENUMERATE fine, COHERE fine, EXECUTE nothing ran, FALSIFY it misses nothing because it is never consulted, CONFORM violates nothing, FEASIBILITY terminates, CONSUME produced no output to consume. It lands nowhere. This is NOT the MEDIUM CHOICE exclusion — medium choice is a candidate REMEDY for this class, not the class. Either add the move (INVOKE — the mechanism is correct and nothing causes it to run) or state why a never-invoked mechanism is out of the set's domain.

findings.title: The BOUNDED residual says what falsifies the set but not how it grows — and supplies an undisciplined dismissal branch beside it
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: CONSUME] The residual's output is `a finding about the SET, recorded as such` — and nothing consumes it: no artifact it is recorded IN, no owner, no path by which the eighth becomes a ninth. Worse, the same paragraph supplies a competing branch with no test: MEDIUM CHOICE is declared outside the domain. A future NONE-classified defect can be routed to either branch on the classifier's word alone, and the walk already exercised the dismissal branch once. Name the recipient of a set finding and state the test distinguishing `a way a mechanism is wrong` from `outside the set's domain`.

findings.title: The `every RULE in Decisions` domain fixes two dispositions but not the annotation vocabulary that expresses them
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] The domain names `a rule annotated SUPERSEDED, or explicitly assigned to another stage`. This change's own explore.md uses at least three forms: SUPERSEDED, OVERTAKEN (added by the walk itself), and `DOMAIN CLOSED … by D-rc13-13` (a LIVE rule whose closure lives in another Decisions entry rather than in Mechanism). An engine keying on the literal word misreads the second; the third reads OPEN forever. Fix the vocabulary where the dispositions are stated: a literal token set declared SOURCED, or a named disposition slot the way `Standing recommendation:` is defined.

findings.title: Run the domain rule on this change's own file: D-rc13-3 and D-rc13-4 read as live-and-open

commentary: MOVE CLASSIFICATION (second held-out test): COHERE 6, ENUMERATE 6, READ 4, EXECUTE 4, CONFORM 2, FALSIFY 1, CONSUME 1, NONE 1. The strongest thing about the current state is that the walk did the expensive thing rather than the cheap one: told its set was not closed, it ran the classification it had skipped, let the answer change the change, and then declined to claim DERIVED for the result. That is the stage's own thesis operating on the stage. What did not travel with it is the edit discipline the change is about. The six-to-eight decision landed in the requirement body and two task lines and stopped — the requirement's own title, its scenario's title, both Impact lists and the Instruments paragraph still say six — and the Mode-B repair edited the WHEN clause the finding named while leaving the THEN in the same scenario scaffolding five sections. Both are the second-copy pattern the first pass diagnosed, recurring INSIDE the repairs for it, which suggests the problem is not that the copies are unknown but that nothing sweeps after an edit lands. The deeper exposure is at the engine seam: rules_open is asserted as engine-computed and then never given anything to compute from — no entry grammar, no decision identifier in the format it reads, no instrument over the parse, and no delta against the capability whose requirement enumerates exactly which explore fields the surface computes. Under that missing delta the change is a fourth capability wide, which is where R-crc-9 becomes live rather than rhetorical — and the change already argued, correctly, that the answer there is to split rather than shrink. On the move scheme: the eight classified almost everything I found, which is a real result for a set assembled from two records; the two places it strained were a defect that is a way a mechanism is wrong before it ever runs (a rule nobody invokes), and a defect about whether the specification can be executed at all rather than about its output. The first has evidence sitting in this change's own Case 8, and the residual as written tells you to record it and then gives you an equally available way to dismiss it.
